text:
rajesh: Noticing an uptick in failed GPU node boots in ap-south-1b since ~10m ago. Warm pool didn't reach target.
lina: Agree, seeing lots of KMS decrypt failures in node bootstrap logs. Example: 
```
2026-03-21T10:12:01Z KMS Decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::999999999999:assumed-role/gpu-provisioner is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource: arn:aws:kms:ap-south-1:999999999999:key/abcd-ef01
```
rajesh: That role hasn't changed in months. Any recent policy pushes?
matt: Security team applied KMS key policy tightening last hour to require aws:PrincipalTag tag:team=infra for decryption (FW-1456). Appears gpu-provisioner role is missing that tag in ap-south.
infra-oncall: Confirmed: policy `restrict-decrypt-to-tag` (rev 3) deployed to customer-managed keystores -> affects our internal keystore-backed disk encryption.
security-bot: Alert: KMS policy change deployed by @lina (changelog fw-1456) at 10:06 UTC.
rajesh: So nodes retry decrypt -> heavy retry loops. NATGW conntrack spiked. Any queue numbers?
sre-bot: NATGW conntrack utilization increased from 32% -> 79% in ap-south-1 within 4m. GPU warmup retry churn detected.
matt: That explains failed image pulls too (signed blobs behind internal proxy requiring decrypted credentials). Whole onboarding path blocked.
lina: Oops, I missed adding the infra tag exception for legacy provisoner roles. My bad. Quick options: 1) revert key policy (risky), 2) add tag to role (safer), 3) add a short-lived KMS grant to gpu-provisioner principal (fast).
rajesh: Short-term: can we apply a KMS Grant for 2h to allow Decrypt for arn:aws:sts::999999999999:assumed-role/gpu-provisioner? That unblocks nodes immediately.
infra-oncall: I can issue a grant now, but grants show in audit logs — compliance needs to sign off.
security-bot: Note: Temporary grants must be logged and approved by compliance within 24h per policy COM-2. I'll create approval request.
sre-bot: After applying grant, warmpool join rate recovered to 95% in ~3m.
rajesh: Good. Now medium-term: we should either tag the role via IaC or update the policy to use `aws:PrincipalOrgID` instead of tags. Which is preferred?
lina: OrgID would be broader and safer for infra roles across accounts. Tags require pulling in multiple repos to ensure roles receive tags before IAM assume. I'm in favor of updating policy to allow a specific organizational principal set + explicit exception for legacy roles via grant transition.
matt: Addendum: audit log volume spiked because every decrypt retry generated an AdminEvent + CloudTrail lookup. Log egress cost estimate ~+$220 for the 6h window for ap-south. Also S3 Put rates climbed due to retryed status writes.
rajesh: Let's open tickets: KMS-298 (policy refactor to OrgID + staged rollout), IAM-611 (tagging playbook for provisioner roles), INFRA-900 (bootstrap grant automation + expiry).
infra-oncall: Also set alert: if NATGW conntrack > 80% in region => rate-limit warmup and disable parallel provisioning. I'll add a circuit breaker to the warmup controller.
security-bot: Compliance: please attach justification to the temporary grant request.
lina: Will attach incident timeline and remediation plan.
sre-bot: Post-incident observation: node churn caused higher CPU on node-manager; autoscaler temporarily overprovisioned by 12% trying to hit desired capacity. Cost impact tracked on ticket INF-COST-112.
rajesh: Follow-ups: 1) backfill tags where possible, 2) policy refactor, 3) automated expiring grants for legacy roles, 4) cool-down on warmup controller. Prioritize KMS-298 and INFRA-900.
matt: Also document runbook: KMS policy deploy checklist must include a canary region (we skipped ap-south this time).
infra-oncall: Done. I've also scheduled a keystore key rotation window at 03:00 UTC tomorrow; postpone if KMS policy refactor isn't complete.
lina: Acknowledged. I'm rolling back the policy on keystore in ap-south only as a stopgap and will file the formal change with timeboxed rollback (30m).
sre-bot: Incident summary: mitigated by temporary grant + regional policy rollback. Root cause = KMS key policy tightened without tagging rollout. Follow-ups assigned: KMS-298, IAM-611, INFRA-900, RUNBOOK-23.
rajesh: Thanks. I'll post a short blurb to #eng-sre and #security with TL;DR and link to tickets. :white_check_mark:
